ACCEPT — PR #7349 (review by the PM session, verified against GitHub, not the report).

**The browser run is real, and the evidence chain holds.** What makes it credible is not the screenshots but the four links between them: `packages/console/dist` was built by `pnpm objectui:build` at the pinned SHA, `dist/.objectui-sha` equals `.objectui-sha`, the served `/_console/` actually requests the freshly built `assets/index-Bn6RZIXn.js`, and the driven session's `GET /api/v1/meta/app` returns `showcase_app` + `account` and **not** `setup`. Each of those closes a way the run could have looked green while proving nothing — a stale dist, a cached bundle, or an admin session wearing a business user's name. Note the third one especially: `check:console-sha` exits 0 when there is no dist at all, so its green alone would not have been evidence.

**The headline check passed, on the artifact that matters.** `approvals:inbox` is present in the built **entry chunk** at module scope, immediately before the app bootstrap. That is precisely the assertion #7231's unit pin states in its own docblock that it cannot make — it runs source, users run the bundle. It is now covered by a checklist item whose first clause is an oracle-`build` assertion, with a source grep explicitly declared insufficient. Good instinct: writing it any other way would have re-created the hole.

Also measured, not inferred: a decision **executed** end to end (server re-read confirms the actor left `pending_approvers`, the action bar was replaced by the server-computed "waiting on…" text, tab count 2→1); `?request=` opens the drawer on **both** routes; the record page renders the server-declared action set rather than the retired hard-coded pair (entry B); Setup lists the inbox above the raw tables; zh reads 待我审批 / 待审批 throughout; and the bell breakdown was exercised **in its clamp case** — button badge `9+`, popover `18 total · 13 notifications + 5 pending approvals`, with M agreeing with Home's card. Nine of ten body checks pass; the tenth is routing-correct and dead-ends on record visibility (#7345).

**A correction I owe, in the open — the second today.** This card's body told you to confirm or refute **#7266**. Triage had already closed that card `not_planned` and moved it to objectui#4074 at 04:33Z, **before** this dispatch, and I did not re-read it when I wrote the card. You confirmed it at the live location instead and said so. The checklist line is satisfied at objectui#4074, not at the stale pointer my card carried.

**Verified independently**: 23 check runs, ESLint / TypeScript Type Check / Check Changeset all `success`, zero failures; `skip-changeset` correctly applied for a `docs/qa`-only change, with `size/m` preserved rather than clobbered. Diff is one file.

**One signal worth carrying into triage on #7347**: this PR's CI was fully green *while* `check:platform-checklist` is red on `main`. So that gate is not in the CI required farm — nothing in CI will catch the pre-existing `coverage.json · qa` breakage, and it will keep failing silently for anyone who runs it locally. Reproducing it on a pristine tree before touching anything, and declining to paper over it because the fix is a ledger-scoping choice, was the right call twice over.

Findings stand as filed for triage to grade: **#7344** (no shipped permission set grants `sys_inbox_message`, so the notification half of the #7213 bell breakdown is structurally 0 for every business user — adjacent to this epic and the one I would grade first), **#7345**, **#7347**, and **objectui#4074**.

Flipping ready and queueing.
